The symmetric behavior (no rectification) with moderate current density at zero bias (1.14 µA/cm²) indicates back-to-back Schottky barriers or interface-dominated transport rather than bulk-limited mechanisms, ruling out simple SCLC. Consider equivalent circuits combining two opposing Schottky diodes in series to represent grain boundary barriers or dual-contact interfaces, which are common in ZnO polycrystalline films. The rejection of Poole-Frenkel and trap SCLC models confirms this is primarily an interface phenomenon rather than bulk trap-limited transport, so focus all future attempts on contact/interface mechanisms with ZnO-appropriate parameters (εr=8.5, electron affinity~4.3 eV).
